strategies.title: Incumbent coordinate ascent
strategies.plan: Keep the seeded Gaussian incumbent as the starting array, but replace its direct return with deterministic lexicographic coordinate ascent on the actual squared ratio. In each of 20 sweeps, test moving each coordinate of each point by both signs of \(h_k=d_{\max}2^{-k}\) for \(k=2,\ldots,12\), recomputing all pairwise distances each time and accepting only the single trial with strictly larger `min_max_ratio`; repeat sweeps until a full sweep has no accepted move. Preserve a copy of the initial seeded array and return it if no trial is accepted, so shape, finiteness, and the 16-point validity requirement are always preserved. This is a local exploitation rather than a replacement construction: every accepted change is directly certified against the evaluator’s exact objective and cannot be harmed by changes in normalization, translation, rotation, or scale. Expected-gain check: every accepted coordinate move has a strictly larger `min_max_ratio` and therefore a strictly larger `combined_score` than 0.0197911238456, while the saved incumbent is a valid fallback if no strict move exists.

strategies.title: Square-grid generator replacement
strategies.plan: Replace the random-point-generation subsystem by the explicit 4-by-4 integer square lattice \(\{(i,j):i,j\in\{0,1,2,3\}\}\), emitted in row-major order. Its nearest-neighbor distance is exactly \(d_{\min}=1\), while its diameter is the opposite-corner distance \(d_{\max}=\sqrt{3^2+3^2}=\sqrt{18}\). Thus its raw `min_max_ratio` is exactly \(1/18\), with no stochastic variation and no optimization dependence. It always returns exactly 16 finite two-dimensional points and is automatically invariant to any harmless evaluator normalization. Expected-gain check: `min_max_ratio` \(=1/18=0.0555555556>0.00153547329022\), so `combined_score` \(=(1/18)/(1/12.889266112)=0.7160703396>0.0197911238456\).

strategies.title: Twelve-plus-four ring packing
strategies.plan: Use a two-scale concentric construction: place 12 points on the unit circle at angles \(2\pi k/12\), \(k=0,\ldots,11\), and place four additional points at \((0.4,0),(-0.4,0),(0,0.4),(0,-0.4)\). The outer ring has diameter 2 and adjacent chord length \(2\sin(\pi/12)=0.5176380902\). The closest outer-to-inner distance is \(1-0.4=0.6\), and the closest inner-to-inner distance is \(0.4\sqrt2\), so the outer adjacent chord is the global minimum distance. This is a structural escape from a rectangular lattice: the twelve hull contacts carry the diameter efficiently while the four interior points occupy otherwise unused central area. Expected-gain check: `min_max_ratio` \(=(0.5176380902/2)^2=\sin^2(\pi/12)=0.0669872981>0.00153547329022\), so `combined_score` \(=0.0669872981\cdot12.889266112=0.863417\ldots>0.0197911238456\).

strategies.title: Incumbent active-contact relaxation
strategies.plan: Start from the current 12-plus-4 coordinates, normalize by their current diameter, and perform a deterministic local maximin relaxation: at each of 200 fixed iterations, move every point by the sum of repulsive vectors from pairs whose distance is within 5% of the current minimum distance, then recenter and rescale to diameter one. Use a geometrically decreasing step size, beginning at 0.01 and halving every 25 iterations, and retain only iterates whose exact squared min/max ratio improves on the best retained iterate. This directly attacks the twelve active neighboring outer-ring contacts while allowing the formerly inactive inner points to move into useful support locations, rather than restricting the geometry to two perfect rings. Include the explicit 11-outer/5-inner construction below as a seed in the retained-candidate pool, so the procedure has a deterministic improving fallback even if the incumbent basin is locally rigid. The expected-gain check is that the fallback has squared ratio approximately 0.07471, hence combined_score approximately \(0.07471/(1/12.889266112)\approx0.963>0.863417\).

strategies.title: Eleven-plus-five coprime rings
strategies.plan: Replace the 12 outer points and 4 axial points by 11 points on the unit circle at angles \(2\pi j/11\), \(j=0,\ldots,10\), and 5 points on an inner regular pentagon. Rotate the pentagon by \(\pi/55\), which places every nearest outer/inner angular separation at exactly \(\pi/55\), the largest possible separation for these coprime ring counts. Set the inner radius to \(r=(-\cos(\pi/55)+\sqrt{\cos^2(\pi/55)+(2\sin(\pi/5))^2-1})/((2\sin(\pi/5))^2-1)\); this makes the nearest cross-ring distance equal to the pentagon side length \(2r\sin(\pi/5)\). The outer-ring nearest-neighbor distance is larger than that common active distance, while the diameter is the largest outer chord \(2\cos(\pi/22)\), so all 16 coordinates are explicit and valid. The expected-gain check is \(d_{\min}/d_{\max}=[2r\sin(\pi/5)]/[2\cos(\pi/22)]\approx0.2733\), giving min_max_ratio approximately 0.07471 and combined_score approximately \(0.963>0.863417\).

strategies.title: Diameter-constrained repulsive packing
strategies.plan: Use a structurally different seed consisting of four staggered rows of four points on a triangular lattice, rescaled to diameter one, then run a fixed deterministic projected force construction. On each of 400 iterations, compute a repulsive displacement \(\sum_{j\ne i}(p_i-p_j)/\max(\|p_i-p_j\|,10^{-8})^3\), subtract the centroid, and uniformly shrink only if the resulting diameter exceeds one; use step sizes \(0.02(0.99)^t\). Preserve the best exact objective seen, and evaluate alongside the explicit eleven-plus-five-ring candidate rather than assuming that the force trajectory must improve monotonically. This explores non-ring, boundary-supported packings with multiple rows and can escape the rotational symmetry ceiling of the incumbent, while every stored candidate is automatically finite, has exactly 16 planar points, and is diameter-normalized. The expected-gain check is that retaining the eleven-plus-five fallback guarantees min_max_ratio approximately 0.07471 and therefore combined_score approximately \(0.963>0.863417\), while any better relaxed lattice iterate replaces it.
